entries.now_source_says: Miguel Cordero (original Mexican grantee, grant of 11 May 1837); Vicente Cordero named in the register is Miguel's son and one of nine heirs, and the lead claimant in the 1879 confirmation petition. Per grant decree printed p73 / Surveyor General cert printed p70
entries.evidence: The GRANT was made to MIGUEL CORDERO, not Vicente. Concession decree printed transcript p73 (PDF p362): 'the citizen, Miguel Cordero, is declared owner in property of the tract of land known by the name of Las Cruces'; Surveyor General Stratton certification printed p70 (PDF p359): 'a true, full and correct copy of the original Espediente of the grant to Miguel Cordero of the Rancho of Las Cruces... Vicente...'. Vicente Cordero is Miguel's SON and one of nine heirs; he (et al) filed the 1879 petition for confirmation

entries.was: María Antonia de la Guerra y Lataillade

entries.evidence: The grant title names the ORIGINAL grantees as Pablo de la Guerra and Juan Cooper, NOT the American claimants in the register. Spanish (stamp p27): 'Por cuanto D. Pablo de la Guerra y D. Juan Cooper han pretendido para sus beneficios personales la mayor parte del terreno conocido con el nombre de Nicacio... he venido en conceder al esperado D. Pablo de la Guerra, diez sitios de ganado mayor... y á D. Juan Cooper por la sesión que hace de cuatro mil pesos que le adeuda el havier Nacional le concedo Seis Sitios de ganado mayor.' English translation (stamp p30-31): granted to 'Don Pablo de la Guerra ten Sitios de ganado Mayor (ten square leagues)... I grant him [Don Juan Cooper] six sitios.' Buckelew' are the U.S. claimants/patentees (Halleck bought de la Guerra's 9 leagues; Cooper's 6 leagues passed via Buckelew/Black — supplemental petition transcript p8, image 8-9).

entries.now_source_says: REJECTED, not Confirmed. The District Court decree of 6 March 1862 (Fletcher M. Haight, US District Judge, Southern District; transcript p226) REVERSED the Board of Land Commissioners' confirmation of 18 Dec 1855 and held the claim invalid. The grant was one of Gov. Pico's 1846 sales/dispositions of former-Mission property (here the San Juan Bautista mission orchard) to pay Mexican wartime supply debts; the DC (following the Larkin line and citing a Nov 14 1845 Mexican ministerial order forbidding alienation of mission property, transcript p28-30) held the sale unauthorized and 'against the express orders of the Mexican government.' The register's/Hoffman 1862's 'confirmed' reflects only the Board's 1855 decision; the case file's final decree (DC, March 1862) governs = rejected
entries.evidence: Board CONFIRMED the claim: opinion by Comm. R. Aug. Thompson delivered Dec 18 1855 (proceedings summary transcript p2-3). BUT the US appealed and the District Court REVERSED and REJECTED it: DC Decree transcript p226 (PDF stamped 226), 'Intermediate Term A.D. 1862, Monterey March 6th 1862... It is Ordered, Adjudged and Decreed that the decision of said Board of Land Commissioners be reversed, and that the said Claim of the Appellee is held as invalid And is hereby Rejected', Fletcher M. Haight US Dist Judge; DC Opinion transcript p228-229 (PDF stamped 228-229): 'The decision of the Board of Commissioners is reversed and the claim is rejected.' Register says 'Confirmed' -- WRONG; final disposition is REJECTED
